title: REHASH reads the configuration file on a tokio worker, and nothing paces the verb
description:
Found by the review of branch irc-verbs, not by the bead that added the
verb (mimid-1wgh.140.4).

Reloader::reload (crates/mimid-agent/src/reload.rs) does synchronous
filesystem work inside its async body: Config::load -> read_config ->
std::fs::File::open and read_to_string of up to MAX_CONFIG_BYTES
(256 KiB), with no spawn_blocking.

A registered IRC connection can drive it as fast as it likes with REHASH
in a loop, blocking a tokio worker on each pass. On a slow or networked
filesystem one open can stall every other IRC and JMAP connection on
that worker. Refusal::AgentConfigReloadRefused rate limits the log line,
not the work.

The size is bounded by a named constant, as AGENTS.md asks; it is the
runtime that is not protected.

Fix: wrap the read in tokio::task::spawn_blocking (the path is already
owned, so a clone and Config::load inside the closure is enough), or
read with tokio::fs and hand the text to Config::parse. If pacing
matters as well, a minimum interval held beside `running` behind the
same mutex answers a too-soon REHASH with the NOTICE instead of a read.

The test is a REHASH loop that must not keep another connection's PING
from being answered.
